key_insight: SL-FAC applies frequency-aware compression to the smashed data (activations/gradients) in split learning, reducing communication volume substantially while preserving model accuracy and training stability.
problem_solved: High communication overhead in split learning caused by transmitting large smashed activations and gradients between many edge devices and the server, which prevents scalable deployment on bandwidth- and resource-constrained devices.
method: Transform smashed data into a frequency domain (e.g., FFT/DCT) and identify/retain the most informative frequency components.
Apply adaptive compression/quantization and selective transmission of low-importance high-frequency components, with lightweight reconstruction at the server.
Integrate the compression pipeline into split learning training to jointly optimize compression rate and task accuracy (low overhead for edge devices).
impact: Enables scalable, bandwidth-efficient split learning for edge devices and multi-client setups, making it practical to train large models across constrained networks with minimal accuracy trade-offs and improved privacy surface.
visual_elements: Split-model diagram: edge device hosting early layers, server hosting remaining layers, arrow showing compressed smashed data transfer
Frequency-spectrum illustration: original vs. compressed (highlighting preserved low-frequency components and removed high-frequency noise)
Bar/line chart: communication volume vs. accuracy comparing baseline SL, quantization-only, and SL-FAC
Pipeline flow: transform → frequency selection → quantize/transmit → reconstruct → backprop (indicating where computation happens)
paper_title: SL-FAC: A Communication-Efficient Split Learning Framework with Frequency-Aware Compression
paper_authors: Zehang Lin, Miao Yang, Haihan Zhu, Zheng Lin, Jianhao Huang
